headline: Interpretable ADMET models and data resources for peptides, macrocycles and drugs
label: Peptide Admet Prediction Resources
summary: New peptide and macrocycle ADMET models, simulated binding data and updated ADMET databases appeared together in November 2026.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning and data infrastructure for ADMET and binding prediction, with peptides and macrocycles as the clearest focus. AIO proposes an interpretable multimodal ADMET framework for cyclic peptides and macrocycles using solvent-aware contrastive pretraining. VReceptor addresses data scarcity by simulating sequence-dependent peptide binding data through pharmacophore-inspired weighting. A JCIM study examines surrogate ADME models trained on synthetic labels across 25 endpoints, with multitask GNNs and uncertainty estimates. ADCdb 2.0 (542 antibody-drug conjugates) and DrugMAP 3.0 extend reference databases with ADMET endpoints. PTM-BDL, HiFiPL-Bench and BFEE3 are adjacent, covering drug-response attribution, scoring-function benchmarking and binding free energy calculation. The summaries do not show the databases being combined with the models.
